days.goalUz: Işlatiladi: Reported Speech — darak, söroq (if / whether) va buyruq (ask / tell + to); say va tell farqi — iş xatlari va xabar yetkaziş.

sections.titleUz: Öqiş: “Şartnomani boy berişiga sal qolgan xat”

exercises.instructionUz: Sözning ma’nosini tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: postpone — keyinga qoldirmoq.
exercises.question: What does “postpone” mean?

exercises.instructionUz: Özlaştirma gapni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: can → could.
exercises.question: “I can help you.” → He said he ___ help me.

exercises.instructionUz: Böş joyga say yoki tell ning töğri şaklini yozing.
exercises.explanationUz: Kişi bor (us) — told.
exercises.text: She ___ us that the price had changed.

exercises.instructionUz: Töğri gapni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Özlaştirilgan söroqda darak tartibi: if I was ready.
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: He asked me was I ready.
He asked me if I was ready.
He asked me if was I ready.
He asked to me if I was ready.

exercises.instructionUz: Gapni ingliz tiliga özlaştirma gap bilan tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: Buyruq: told + kişi + to + fe’l.
exercises.source: Rahbar menga hisobotni juma kunigaça yuborişni aytdi.
accepted: The manager told me to send the report by Friday
My manager told me to send the report by Friday
The boss told me to send the report by Friday
The manager asked me to send the report by Friday

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlardan özlaştirma söroq gap tuzing.
exercises.explanationUz: asked + kişi + wh-söz + ega + fe’l: She asked me where I worked.

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlarni tarjimasi bilan boğlang.
exercises.explanationUz: deny — inkor etmoq, confirm — tasdiqlamoq, complaint — şikoyat, deal — bitim.

exercises.instructionUz: Grammatik qoida haqidagi fikr töğrimi (true) yoki xatomi (false)?
exercises.explanationUz: Gap hali ham töğri bölsa (ofis hali ham soat 9 da oçiladi), zamonni özgartirmaslik mumkin. Fikr töğri.
exercises.statement: If something is still true, we can keep the present tense: “He said the office opens at nine.”

days.goalUz: Işlatiladi: Relative Clauses — who / which / that / whose / where, aniqlovçi va izohlovçi ergaş gaplar, olmoşni taşlab ketiş — texnologiya va startaplar haqida.

exercises.instructionUz: Sözning ma’nosini tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: affordable — hamyonbop.
exercises.question: What does “affordable” mean?

exercises.instructionUz: Mos olmoşni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Egalik — whose.
exercises.question: The student ___ project won the competition is from Navoi.

exercises.instructionUz: Böş joyga mos olmoşni yozing.
exercises.explanationUz: Joy — where.
exercises.text: This is the office ___ the app was designed.

exercises.instructionUz: Töğri gapni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Izohlovçi gapda narsa uçun which; that va who işlatilmaydi, it takrorlanmaydi.
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: My laptop, that I bought in May, is broken.
My laptop, who I bought in May, is broken.
My laptop, which I bought in May, is broken.
My laptop, which I bought it in May, is broken.

exercises.instructionUz: Gapni ingliz tiliga tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: “… bilan işlaydigan odamlar” — people who work with …
exercises.source: Kompyuter bilan işlaydigan odamlar köp dam olişi kerak.
accepted: People who work with computers should rest a lot
People who work with computers need to rest a lot
People who work on computers should rest a lot
People that work with computers should rest a lot

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlardan gap tuzing.
exercises.explanationUz: ot + (that) + ega + fe’l: The phone I bought is light.

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlarni tarjimasi bilan boğlang.
exercises.explanationUz: launch — işga tuşirmoq, feature — xususiyat, investor — sarmoyador, privacy — maxfiylik.

exercises.instructionUz: Grammatik qoida haqidagi fikr töğrimi (true) yoki xatomi (false)?
exercises.explanationUz: Olmoş EGA bölganda taşlab bölmaydi: The man who called … Fikr xato.
exercises.statement: We can always leave out “who” in “The man who called you is here.”

days.goalUz: Işlatiladi: Third Conditional (if + had + V3, would have + V3), should have / could have / might have — ötmişdagi qarorlar va ularning oqibatlari.

exercises.instructionUz: Sözning ma’nosini tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: drought — qurğoqçilik.
exercises.question: What does “drought” mean?

exercises.instructionUz: Mos şaklni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Ötmişdagi natija — would have + V3.
exercises.question: If we had taken a map, we ___ lost.

exercises.instructionUz: Fe’lni töğri şaklda yozing (should have + V3).
exercises.explanationUz: should have + V3: should have gone.
exercises.text: You look ill. You ___ (go) to bed earlier.

exercises.instructionUz: Töğri gapni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: If + had + V3, … would have + V3.
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: If it hadn’t rained, we would have played.
If it wouldn’t have rained, we would have played.
If it didn’t rain, we would have played.
If it hadn’t rained, we would played.

exercises.instructionUz: Gapni ingliz tiliga tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: “… mumkin edi” — could have + V3.
exercises.source: Bu juda yomonroq bölişi mumkin edi.
accepted: It could have been much worse
This could have been much worse
It could have been a lot worse
It could have been far worse

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlardan gap tuzing.
exercises.explanationUz: ega + shouldn’t have + V3 + …

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlarni tarjimasi bilan boğlang.
exercises.explanationUz: prevent — oldini olmoq, consequence — oqibat, restore — tiklamoq, flood — toşqin.

exercises.instructionUz: Grammatik qoida haqidagi fikr töğrimi (true) yoki xatomi (false)?
exercises.explanationUz: “I’d gone” = I had gone; “I’d have gone” = I would have gone. Fikr töğri.
exercises.statement: In “If I’d known, I’d have helped”, the first ’d means “had” and the second means “would”.

days.goalUz: Işlatiladi: Past Simple, Past Continuous, Past Perfect, Past Perfect Continuous; when / while / by the time — sayohat hikoyasini izçil aytib beriş va yoziş.

exercises.instructionUz: Sözning ma’nosini tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: hospitality — mehmondöstlik.
exercises.question: What does “hospitality” mean?

exercises.instructionUz: Mos zamonni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Fon jarayon — was raining.
exercises.question: It ___ heavily when we left the hotel.

exercises.instructionUz: Fe’lni Past Perfect şaklida yozing.
exercises.explanationUz: Avvalroq bölgan voqea: had forgotten.
exercises.text: At the airport I realised that I ___ (forget) my charger.

exercises.instructionUz: Töğri gapni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Know — holat fe’li: I knew (I was knowing — xato).
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: I was knowing nobody in the city.
I knew nobody in the city.
I was know nobody in the city.

exercises.instructionUz: Gapni ingliz tiliga tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: “… yetib kelgunimizça … yopilgan edi” — By the time we arrived, … had closed.
exercises.source: Biz yetib kelgunimizça muzey yopilgan edi.
accepted: By the time we arrived, the museum had closed
By the time we got there, the museum had closed
When we arrived, the museum had closed
By the time we arrived the museum had closed
When we arrived, the museum had already closed

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlardan gap tuzing.
exercises.explanationUz: ega + had been + V-ing + for …

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlarni tarjimasi bilan boğlang.
exercises.explanationUz: luggage — yuk, stranger — notaniş odam, delay — keçikiş, eventually — oxir-oqibat.

exercises.instructionUz: Grammatik qoida haqidagi fikr töğrimi (true) yoki xatomi (false)?
exercises.explanationUz: Before / after bilan tartib aniq bölsa, Past Simple ham yetarli. Fikr töğri.
exercises.statement: In “After we ate, we walked to the square”, the Past Perfect is not necessary.

days.goalUz: Işlatiladi: gerund va infinitive andozalari (avoid / suggest + -ing, afford / refuse + to, remember / stop / try farqi, it’s worth -ing) — pul, byudjet va firibgarlikdan saqlaniş haqida.

sections.titleUz: Öqiş: “Yoş oila byudjet tuzişni qanday örgandi”

exercises.instructionUz: Sözning ma’nosini tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: income — daromad.
exercises.question: What does “income” mean?

exercises.instructionUz: Mos şaklni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Consider + -ing.
exercises.question: Have you considered ___ a cheaper phone plan?

exercises.instructionUz: Fe’lni töğri şaklda yozing.
exercises.explanationUz: Refuse + to: refused to sign.
exercises.text: He ___ (refuse) ___ (sign) the contract.

exercises.instructionUz: Töğri gapni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Look forward to + -ing.
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: I look forward to hear from you.
I look forward to hearing from you.
I look forward hearing from you.
I look forward for hearing from you.

exercises.instructionUz: Gapni ingliz tiliga tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: “Qurbimiz yetmaydi” — can’t afford to.
exercises.source: Biz yangi maşina olişga qurbimiz yetmaydi.
accepted: We can’t afford to buy a new car
We can't afford to buy a new car
We cannot afford to buy a new car
We can’t afford a new car

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlardan gap tuzing.
exercises.explanationUz: avoid + -ing.

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlarni tarjimasi bilan boğlang.
exercises.explanationUz: loan — kredit, savings — jamğarma, scam — firibgarlik, budget — byudjet.

exercises.instructionUz: Grammatik qoida haqidagi fikr töğrimi (true) yoki xatomi (false)?
exercises.explanationUz: “I stopped to buy bread” — non sotib oliş uçun töxtadim; “stopped buying” — sotib olişni taşladim. Ma’no farq qiladi — fikr xato.
exercises.statement: “I stopped to buy bread” and “I stopped buying bread” mean the same.

days.goalUz: Işlatiladi: wish / if only + Past Simple, Past Perfect, would va could; wish va hope farqi — jamiyatdagi muammolar, köngillilik va afsus haqida.

exercises.instructionUz: Sözning ma’nosini tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: volunteer — köngilli.
exercises.question: What does “volunteer” mean?

exercises.instructionUz: Mos şaklni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Hozirgi istak — Past Simple (lived).
exercises.question: I wish my best friend ___ in the same city.

exercises.instructionUz: Fe’lni töğri şaklda yozing.
exercises.explanationUz: Ötmişdagi afsus — had + V3: had taken.
exercises.text: I wish I ___ (take) more photos at my sister’s wedding.

exercises.instructionUz: Töğri gapni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Özimiz haqida would emas, could: I wish I could …
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: I wish I would speak Chinese.
I wish I could speak Chinese.
I wish I can speak Chinese.
I wish I will speak Chinese.

exercises.instructionUz: Gapni ingliz tiliga tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: Boşqa odamning odati — wish + would (not).
exercises.source: Qaniydi, odamlar köçaga axlat taşlamasa.
accepted: I wish people wouldn’t throw rubbish in the street
I wish people wouldn't throw rubbish in the street
I wish people would not throw rubbish in the street
I wish people wouldn’t throw rubbish on the street
If only people wouldn’t throw rubbish in the street

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlardan gap tuzing.
exercises.explanationUz: wish + ega + would + fe’l.

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlarni tarjimasi bilan boğlang.
exercises.explanationUz: community — jamoa, donate — xayriya qilmoq, fair — adolatli, pressure — bosim.

exercises.instructionUz: Grammatik qoida haqidagi fikr töğrimi (true) yoki xatomi (false)?
exercises.explanationUz: Ertangi imtihon — real kelajak: hope. Wish bu yerda xato. Fikr töğri.
exercises.statement: We say “I hope you pass your exam tomorrow”, not “I wish you passed”.

days.goalUz: Işlatiladi: Future Continuous (will be + V-ing), Future Perfect (will have + V3), by + vaqt — kelajak rejalari, maqsadlar va başoratlar haqida.

sections.titleUz: Gapiriş: ön yil, şahar, kelasi hafta

exercises.instructionUz: Sözning ma’nosini tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: priority — ustuvor vazifa.
exercises.question: What does “priority” mean?

exercises.instructionUz: Mos şaklni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: By + vaqtgaça tugagan — will have + V3.
exercises.question: By Monday, the builders ___ the new bridge.

exercises.instructionUz: Fe’lni Future Continuous şaklida yozing.
exercises.explanationUz: will be + V-ing: will be travelling.
exercises.text: Don’t visit us in July — we ___ (travel) around Europe.

exercises.instructionUz: Töğri gapni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Will have + V3 (gone).
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: By ten, everyone will have went home.
By ten, everyone will have gone home.
By ten, everyone will gone home.
By ten, everyone will be gone home already.

exercises.instructionUz: Gapni ingliz tiliga tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: “Aynan şu paytda … ayotgan bölaman” — This time … I will be + V-ing.
exercises.source: Ertaga aynan şu paytda men imtihon topşirayotgan bölaman.
accepted: This time tomorrow I will be taking an exam
This time tomorrow I will be taking my exam
At this time tomorrow I will be taking an exam
This time tomorrow I’ll be taking an exam
Tomorrow at this time I will be taking an exam

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlardan muloyim söroq tuzing.
exercises.explanationUz: Will + ega + be + V-ing …?

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlarni tarjimasi bilan boğlang.
exercises.explanationUz: goal — maqsad, predict — başorat qilmoq, graduate — öqişni tamomlamoq, long-term — uzoq muddatli.

exercises.instructionUz: Grammatik qoida haqidagi fikr töğrimi (true) yoki xatomi (false)?
exercises.explanationUz: “Will you be using …?” odatda “Will you use …?” dan muloyimroq eşitiladi. Fikr töğri.
exercises.statement: “Will you be using the car?” sounds more polite than “Will you use the car?”.

vocab.explanationEn: To discuss something formally in order to reach an agreement.
vocab.exampleEn: We negotiated a lower price with the supplier.
vocab.exampleUz: Yetkazib beruvçi bilan arzonroq narxga kelişdik.

vocab.explanationEn: Comments about how well someone has done something, given to help them improve.
vocab.exampleEn: My manager gave me useful feedback on my presentation.
vocab.exampleUz: Rahbarim taqdimotim haqida foydali fikr bildirdi.

vocab.explanationEn: To say that something is true, although it has not been proved.
vocab.exampleEn: The supplier claimed that the goods had been sent.
vocab.exampleUz: Yetkazib beruvçi tovarlar jönatilganini ta’kidladi.

vocab.explanationEn: To say that something is not true.
vocab.exampleEn: He denied that he had lost the documents.
vocab.exampleUz: U hujjatlarni yöqotganini inkor etdi.

vocab.explanationEn: To make someone remember something they must do.
vocab.exampleEn: Please remind me to call the bank at three.
vocab.exampleUz: Iltimos, soat uçda bankka qöngiroq qilişni eslating.

vocab.explanationEn: A list of things to discuss at a meeting.
vocab.exampleEn: The first item on the agenda is the budget.
vocab.exampleUz: Kun tartibidagi birinçi masala — byudjet.

vocab.explanationEn: To arrange for an event to happen later than planned.
vocab.exampleEn: The meeting was postponed until next week.
vocab.exampleUz: Majlis keyingi haftaga qoldirildi.

vocab.explanationEn: A situation where someone does not understand something correctly.
vocab.exampleEn: The delay was caused by a misunderstanding.
vocab.exampleUz: Keçikişga anglaşilmovçilik sabab böldi.

vocab.explanationEn: Behaving in a way that shows respect for other people.
vocab.exampleEn: Always be polite to customers, even when they are angry.
vocab.exampleUz: Mijozlar jahli çiqqan bölsa ham, ular bilan doim xuşmuomala böling.

vocab.explanationEn: To say or show that something is definitely true or will happen.
vocab.exampleEn: Could you confirm the date of the delivery?
vocab.exampleUz: Yetkaziş sanasini tasdiqlay olasizmi?

vocab.explanationEn: A statement that you are unhappy about something.
vocab.exampleEn: We received three complaints about the late orders.
vocab.exampleUz: Keçikkan buyurtmalar haqida uçta şikoyat oldik.

vocab.explanationEn: A business agreement.
vocab.exampleEn: The two companies signed a deal worth two million dollars.
vocab.exampleUz: Ikki kompaniya ikki million dollarlik bitim imzoladi.

vocab.explanationEn: A new idea, method or product.
vocab.exampleEn: Mobile banking was the biggest innovation of the decade.
vocab.exampleUz: Mobil banking ön yillikning eng katta yangiligi böldi.

vocab.explanationEn: A small new business, often in technology.
vocab.exampleEn: She works for a start-up that makes educational apps.
vocab.exampleUz: U ta’lim ilovalari yaratadigan startapda işlaydi.

vocab.explanationEn: A person or organisation that puts money into a business to make a profit.
vocab.exampleEn: Two investors have already put money into the project.
vocab.exampleUz: Ikki investor loyihaga allaqaçon pul kiritdi.

vocab.explanationEn: To start selling a new product or service.
vocab.exampleEn: The company launched its app in three cities.
vocab.exampleUz: Kompaniya ilovasini uçta şaharda işga tuşirdi.

vocab.explanationEn: A person who uses a product, machine or service.
vocab.exampleEn: The app has 50,000 active users.
vocab.exampleUz: Ilovaning 50 000 faol foydalanuvçisi bor.

vocab.explanationEn: An important part or function of a product.
vocab.exampleEn: The best feature of this phone is the camera.
vocab.exampleUz: Bu telefonning eng yaxşi xususiyati — kamerasi.

vocab.explanationEn: Working well without wasting time, money or energy.
vocab.exampleEn: Solar panels are becoming more efficient every year.
vocab.exampleUz: Quyoş panellari yil sayin samaraliroq bölmoqda.

vocab.explanationEn: An important discovery or development.
vocab.exampleEn: Scientists have made a breakthrough in battery technology.
vocab.exampleUz: Olimlar batareya texnologiyasida katta yutuqqa erişişdi.

vocab.explanationEn: Cheap enough for most people to buy.
vocab.exampleEn: The aim is to make internet access affordable for villages.
vocab.exampleUz: Maqsad — internetni qişloqlar uçun hamyonbop qiliş.

vocab.explanationEn: To need something in order to work or survive.
vocab.exampleEn: Many farmers now rely on weather apps.
vocab.exampleUz: Köp fermerlar endi ob-havo ilovalariga tayanadi.

vocab.explanationEn: The right to keep your personal information secret.
vocab.exampleEn: Users are worried about their privacy online.
vocab.exampleUz: Foydalanuvçilar internetdagi maxfiyligi haqida xavotirda.

vocab.explanationEn: A person or company that creates software or new products.
vocab.exampleEn: The developers who built the app are only twenty-two.
vocab.exampleUz: Ilovani yaratgan dasturçilar endigina yigirma ikki yoşda.

vocab.explanationEn: A long period with little or no rain.
vocab.exampleEn: The drought destroyed half of the harvest.
vocab.exampleUz: Qurğoqçilik hosilning yarmini nobud qildi.

vocab.explanationEn: Supplying water to land so that crops can grow.
vocab.exampleEn: Most river water is used for irrigation.
vocab.exampleUz: Daryo suvining köp qismi suğorişga işlatiladi.

vocab.explanationEn: A result of an action, often a bad one.
vocab.exampleEn: Nobody thought about the long-term consequences.
vocab.exampleUz: Heç kim uzoq muddatli oqibatlar haqida öylamadi.

vocab.explanationEn: To become smaller.
vocab.exampleEn: The lake has shrunk to half its size.
vocab.exampleUz: Köl ikki baravar kiçrayib ketdi.

vocab.explanationEn: A large amount of water covering land that is usually dry.
vocab.exampleEn: The flood damaged hundreds of homes.
vocab.exampleUz: Toşqin yuzlab uylarga zarar yetkazdi.

vocab.explanationEn: To stop something from happening.
vocab.exampleEn: Planting trees can prevent soil erosion.
vocab.exampleUz: Daraxt ekiş tuproq eroziyasining oldini olişi mumkin.

vocab.explanationEn: To feel sorry about something you did or did not do.
vocab.exampleEn: I regret not taking the train.
vocab.exampleUz: Poyezdda bormaganimdan afsuslanaman.

vocab.explanationEn: Very small pieces of dry earth or dirt.
vocab.exampleEn: Strong winds carry dust and salt for hundreds of kilometres.
vocab.exampleUz: Kuçli şamollar çang va tuzni yuzlab kilometrga olib ketadi.

vocab.explanationEn: A statement that something bad may happen.
vocab.exampleEn: Scientists gave a warning years ago, but nobody listened.
vocab.exampleUz: Olimlar yillar oldin ogohlantirgan, lekin heç kim quloq solmagan.

vocab.explanationEn: To bring something back to its earlier good condition.
vocab.exampleEn: The project aims to restore the forest.
vocab.exampleUz: Loyiha örmonni tiklaşni maqsad qilgan.

vocab.explanationEn: A plant grown by farmers, such as wheat or cotton.
vocab.exampleEn: Cotton needs a lot of water compared with other crops.
vocab.exampleUz: Paxta boşqa ekinlarga qaraganda köp suv talab qiladi.

vocab.explanationEn: Possible to prevent.
vocab.exampleEn: Many of these problems were avoidable.
vocab.exampleUz: Bu muammolarning köpini oldini oliş mumkin edi.

vocab.explanationEn: An occasion when you travel from one place to another, especially a long distance.
vocab.exampleEn: The journey from Tashkent to Nukus takes about twenty hours by train.
vocab.exampleUz: Toşkentdan Nukusgaça poyezdda safar taxminan yigirma soat davom etadi.

vocab.explanationEn: The place where someone is going.
vocab.exampleEn: Samarkand is a popular destination for tourists.
vocab.exampleUz: Samarqand sayyohlar uçun maşhur manzil.

vocab.explanationEn: The bags and cases that you take when you travel.
vocab.exampleEn: My luggage didn’t arrive with the plane.
vocab.exampleUz: Yukim samolyot bilan birga kelmadi.

vocab.explanationEn: To get on a plane, train, ship or bus.
vocab.exampleEn: Passengers can now board the train.
vocab.exampleUz: Yölovçilar endi poyezdga çiqişi mumkin.

vocab.explanationEn: A situation in which something happens later than expected.
vocab.exampleEn: There was a three-hour delay because of the snow.
vocab.exampleUz: Qor tufayli uç soatlik keçikiş böldi.

vocab.explanationEn: A person you do not know.
vocab.exampleEn: A stranger helped me find my hotel.
vocab.exampleUz: Notaniş bir odam mehmonxonamni topişga yordam berdi.

vocab.explanationEn: Friendly and generous behaviour towards guests.
vocab.exampleEn: Uzbek hospitality is famous all over the world.
vocab.exampleUz: Özbek mehmondöstligi butun dunyoga maşhur.

vocab.explanationEn: To become unable to find your way.
vocab.exampleEn: We got lost in the narrow streets of the old city.
vocab.exampleUz: Eski şaharning tor köçalarida adaşib qoldik.

vocab.explanationEn: Money that you owe to someone.

vocab.explanationEn: Money that you earn from work or investments.

vocab.explanationEn: To use or spend less of something.

vocab.explanationEn: A strong wish to achieve something.

vocab.explanationEn: To finish something by the time it must be finished.

vocab.explanationEn: To succeed in doing something difficult.

vocab.explanationEn: To finish a course at a university or college.

grammar.titleEn: Reported speech: statements, questions and requests
explanationUz: Özlaştirma gap — boşqa odamning sözlarini aynan emas, öz sözimiz bilan yetkaziş: “I am busy,” she said. → She said (that) she was busy. Odatda zamon bir qadam ortga suriladi: Present Simple → Past Simple, Present Perfect → Past Perfect, will → would, can → could.

Vaqt va joy sözlari ham özgaradi: today → that day, tomorrow → the next day / the following day, yesterday → the day before, here → there, this → that. Agar gap hali ham töğri bölsa, zamonni özgartirmaslik ham mumkin: He said the office opens at nine.

Söroq gaplarda söz tartibi DARAK gapdagidek böladi, söroq belgisi va do / did işlatilmaydi: “Where do you work?” → She asked me where I worked. Ha / yöq savollarda if yoki whether: “Have you signed the contract?” → He asked if I had signed the contract.

Buyruq va iltimoslar tell / ask + kişi + to + fe’l bilan beriladi: “Please send the report.” → She asked me to send the report. Inkor: tell somebody not to do: He told us not to be late. Say’dan keyin kişi kelmaydi (She said me — xato), tell’dan keyin esa kişi şart (She told me).

formula.form: say (that) + ega + zamon bir qadam ortga
formula.noteUz: “We will win.” → They said they would win.
He told me (that) the deal was ready.
She asked where the office was. He asked if I could help.
The manager told us not to postpone the meeting.

explanationUz: Aniqlovçi (defining) ergaş gap QAYSI odam yoki narsa haqida gap ketayotganini aniqlaydi va vergulsiz yoziladi: The app that I use for banking is very fast. Odamlar uçun who (yoki that), narsalar uçun which (yoki that), egalik uçun whose, joy uçun where işlatiladi.

Izohlovçi (non-defining) ergaş gap QÖŞIMÇA ma’lumot beradi, uni olib taşlasa ham gap tuşunarli qoladi; vergul bilan ajratiladi va unda that işlatilmaydi: IT Park, which opened in 2019, now has hundreds of companies. My sister, who is a developer, works from home.

Aniqlovçi ergaş gapda olmoş TÖLDIRUVÇI bölsa, uni taşlab ketiş mumkin: The phone (that) I bought last week has a great camera. Lekin olmoş EGA bölsa, taşlab bölmaydi: The man who founded the company is my neighbour (“The man founded the company …” — boşqa ma’no).

Which butun oldingi gapga ham işora qiliş mumkin: The app crashed twice, which annoyed the users. Old qöşimçali şakllar rasmiy uslubda: the investor to whom we spoke; oğzaki nutqda: the investor (who) we spoke to.

grammar.titleUz: Third Conditional va should have / could have
grammar.titleEn: Third conditional; should have / could have
explanationUz: Third Conditional — ÖTMIŞDA sodir bölmagan, endi özgartirib bölmaydigan xayoliy şart: If we had left earlier, we would have caught the train. (Erta çiqmadik, poyezdga ulgurmadik.) Özbekçada “… ganimizda, … gan bölardik” şakliga mos.

Tuzilma: If + had + V3 (Past Perfect), … would have + V3. Natijada could have (imkoniyat) va might have (ehtimol) ham keladi: If they had planted trees, the dust storms might have been weaker. Qisqartmalarni çalkaştirmang: I’d gone = I had gone, I’d have gone = I would have gone.

Should have + V3 — ötmişdagi xato uçun tanqid yoki afsus: We should have saved more water (saqlamadik — xato qildik). Shouldn’t have + V3 — qilinmasligi kerak bölgan iş: They shouldn’t have built the factory so close to the river.

Could have + V3 — ötmişda imkoniyat bölgan, lekin foydalanilmagan: The flood could have been much worse (yaxşiyamki, yomonroq bölmadi). Bu şakllarda have dan keyin doim V3 keladi: should have gone (should have went — xato).

formula.form: If + had + V3, ega + would have + V3
formula.noteUz: If I had known, I would have helped.

formula.form: ega + would have + V3 + if + had + V3
formula.noteUz: We would have arrived on time if the road hadn’t been closed.

grammar.titleUz: Hikoya zamonlari: Past Simple, Continuous, Perfect
explanationUz: Hikoyaning asosiy voqealari ketma-ket Past Simple’da aytiladi: We arrived, left our bags and went out. Past Continuous (was / were + V-ing) esa fon, ya’ni voqea paytida davom etayotgan jarayonni beradi: It was raining and people were hurrying home when we arrived.

Past Perfect (had + V3) — hikoyadagi ötgan nuqtadan HAM OLDIN bölgan voqea: When we got to the station, the train had already left (poyezd biz kelişimizdan oldin ketgan). Ikki voqea tartibi aniq bölsa (before, after), Past Simple ham yetarli: After we had eaten / After we ate, we walked to the square.

Past Perfect Continuous (had been + V-ing) — ötgan nuqtagaça QANÇA VAQT davom etgan jarayon: We had been waiting for three hours when the bus finally came. Köpinça sabab yoki natija bilan keladi: She was tired because she had been travelling all day.

Hikoyada vaqt bağlovçilari muhim: when, while, as soon as, by the time, until. While odatda Past Continuous bilan: While I was taking photos, someone stole my bag. By the time + Past Simple, … had + V3: By the time we reached the hotel, the restaurant had closed.

explanationUz: Ayrim fe’llardan keyin -ing (gerund) keladi: avoid, enjoy, mind, consider, suggest, keep, finish, can’t stand, give up. I avoid using my credit card. She suggested opening a savings account. Old qöşimçalardan keyin ham doim -ing: She is good at saving money. Thank you for helping me.

Boşqa fe’llardan keyin to + fe’l (infinitive) keladi: afford, decide, plan, hope, agree, refuse, manage, promise, want, need, learn. We can’t afford to travel this year. He refused to lend me money. Sifatdan keyin ham to: It’s easy to spend too much.

Ayrim fe’llar ikki şaklda keladi, lekin MA’NO özgaradi. Remember to do — bajariş kerakligini eslamoq (Remember to pay the rent!); remember doing — qilganini eslamoq (I remember paying it). Stop to do — biror işni qiliş uçun töxtamoq; stop doing — qilişni taşlamoq (I stopped buying coffee every day). Try to do — urinmoq; try doing — sinab körmoq.

Ma’no deyarli özgarmaydigan fe’llar: like, love, hate, prefer, start, begin, continue — I like cooking / I like to cook. Ibora: It’s worth + -ing (It’s worth checking your bank statement), There’s no point + -ing (There’s no point worrying about it).

grammar.titleUz: Wish va If only: istak va afsus
explanationUz: Hozirgi holatdan norozilik yoki istak: wish + Past Simple. I wish I had more free time (hozir böş vaqtim yöq). If only = wish, lekin kuçliroq his bildiradi: If only my grandmother lived closer! Be fe’li bilan rasmiy uslubda were: I wish I were taller.

Ötmişdagi voqeadan afsus: wish + Past Perfect (had + V3). I wish I had studied harder at school (öqimadim — endi afsusdaman). If only we hadn’t sold the old house! Bu Third Conditional’ga öxşaydi: ötmişni özgartirib bölmaydi.

Boşqa odamning xatti-harakatidan norozilik va uning özgarişini istaş: wish + would + fe’l. I wish my brother would stop using his phone at dinner. Özimiz haqida would işlatilmaydi: I wish I would … emas, I wish I could … (imkoniyat): I wish I could speak Korean.

Hope bilan çalkaştirmang: hope — real, ehtimoli bor narsa uçun (I hope it doesn’t rain tomorrow), wish — xayoliy, real bölmagan narsa uçun (I wish it weren’t raining now). “I wish you a happy birthday” — boşqa ma’no: tilak bildiriş.

explanationUz: Future Continuous (will be + V-ing) — kelajakdagi ANIQ BIR PAYTDA davom etayotgan iş: This time tomorrow I will be flying to Istanbul. At eight o’clock tonight we’ll be watching the match. Özbekçada “… ayotgan bölaman” şakliga mos.

Future Continuous rejalaştirilgan, odatiy işni muloyim söraş uçun ham işlatiladi: Will you be using the car this evening? (= Agar kerak bölmasa, men olsam bölarmidi?) Bu oddiy “Will you use …?” dan yumşoqroq eşitiladi.

Future Perfect (will have + V3) — kelajakdagi bir nuqtagaça TUGAGAN iş: By 2030 I will have graduated. By the time you arrive, I’ll have cooked dinner. Köpinça by + vaqt (by Friday, by the end of the year, by then) bilan keladi; inkor: won’t have + V3.

Future Perfect Continuous (will have been + V-ing) — kelajakdagi nuqtagaça qança vaqt davom etgan bölişi: In June I will have been working here for five years. B2 darajasida asosan tanib oliş kifoya, lekin u davomiylikni ta’kidlaşini esda tuting.

reading.title: The Email That Nearly Cost a Contract
paragraphs: Last spring a textile company in Namangan almost lost its biggest client because of a single email. The buyer, a clothing brand in Poland, had asked whether the company could deliver ten thousand shirts by the end of May. A young sales manager replied that it would be “no problem”, without checking with the factory. Two weeks later the production team told him that they could not finish before the middle of June.

When the manager wrote to the client again, he simply said that there had been “a small delay”. The Polish buyer was furious. In a long reply, she said that her shops had already advertised the new collection and that the company had given her false information. She asked why nobody had warned her earlier and demanded a fifteen percent discount.

The director, Ravshan Aliev, decided to call the client himself. He admitted that his team had made a mistake and explained exactly what had happened. He offered to send the first three thousand shirts by air at the company’s cost. The buyer accepted, and the two companies are still working together. “The delay wasn’t the real problem,” Aliev told his staff afterwards. “The problem was that we promised something we hadn’t checked. Clients forgive bad news, but they don’t forgive surprises.”

reading.title: The App That Taught a Village to Sell Online
paragraphs: Three years ago Shahzoda Umarova, who had just graduated in computer science, returned to her home village in the Fergana Valley. She noticed that the women who made embroidered suzani were selling them to traders for very low prices. The traders, who took the products to Tashkent, earned up to five times more than the women themselves.

Shahzoda decided to build a simple app that would connect the craftswomen directly with buyers. The first version, which she wrote in her bedroom in two months, allowed users to upload photos, set prices and receive orders. Its most important feature was a voice-message function for women whose reading skills were weak. Within a year, forty women from four villages were selling through the app, and their income had almost doubled.

The project attracted an investor from Almaty whose company helps rural businesses. With his money, Shahzoda hired two developers and added online payments and delivery tracking. Not everything has gone smoothly. Some older buyers do not trust online payments, and the delivery service, which is run by a small local firm, is sometimes slow. Still, Shahzoda believes that technology works best when it solves a real problem for people who were previously left out.

reading.title: What Could Have Saved the Aral Sea?
paragraphs: In the 1960s the Aral Sea was one of the largest lakes in the world, and the town of Muynak was a busy fishing port. Then planners decided to use the water of its two great rivers, the Amu Darya and the Syr Darya, to irrigate huge cotton fields. Within a few decades the sea had lost most of its water. Today Muynak is more than a hundred kilometres from the shore, and old fishing boats lie rusting in the sand.

Many experts say that the disaster was avoidable. If the irrigation canals had been built properly, much less water would have been lost on the way to the fields. If farmers had grown crops that needed less water, the rivers might still have reached the sea. Some scientists warned about the consequences as early as the 1970s, but their warnings were ignored. “We should have listened to them,” says Bakhtiyor, a retired teacher from Nukus. “My father lost his job as a fisherman, and my children grew up breathing dust and salt.”

Not everything is lost, however. In the north, Kazakhstan built a dam that has helped the Small Aral to recover, and fish have returned. On the dry seabed in Uzbekistan, millions of saxaul trees have been planted to hold the sand in place. These projects cannot restore the sea to what it was, but they show that it is never too late to reduce the damage.

reading.title: The Night I Missed the Last Train
paragraphs: Lucy, a student from Manchester, had been travelling around Uzbekistan for two weeks when her plans suddenly went wrong. She had spent the day in Shakhrisabz and was planning to take the evening train back to Samarkand. She had bought her ticket online the day before, so she wasn’t worried. But when she reached the station, the platform was empty. The train had left an hour earlier — she had been reading the timetable for the wrong day.

It was getting dark and her phone battery was almost dead. While she was trying to find a taxi, an elderly woman who had been selling apricots outside the station asked her if she needed help. Lucy didn’t speak Uzbek and the woman knew only a few words of English, but with gestures and a translation app they managed to understand each other. The woman, whose name was Gulsara, insisted that Lucy should stay the night at her house.

That evening was the highlight of Lucy’s whole trip. Gulsara’s family had already eaten, but they cooked a fresh plov for their guest, and the grandchildren practised their school English with her until midnight. The next morning Gulsara’s son drove her to the bus station and refused to take any money. “I had read a lot about Uzbek hospitality before I came,” Lucy wrote later on her blog, “but I hadn’t imagined anything like this. Missing that train was the best mistake I have ever made.”

reading.title: How a Young Couple Learned to Budget
paragraphs: When Sherzod and Madina got married, they both had good jobs in Tashkent, but at the end of every month their bank cards were almost empty. “We kept asking ourselves where the money had gone,” Madina says. “We weren’t buying anything expensive, but we never managed to save anything.”

A friend who works in a bank suggested writing down every expense for one month. The result shocked them. They had spent more on taxis and food delivery than on rent. Small impulse buys — a phone case here, a new scarf there — added up to a large sum. They decided to make a simple budget: a fixed amount for food, transport and fun, and ten percent of their income went straight into a savings account on payday.

The first months were difficult. Sherzod admits that he hated taking the bus instead of a taxi, and Madina missed ordering pizza on Friday nights. But they kept going, and after a year they had saved enough for a small car without taking a loan. Their advice to other young couples is simple: “Don’t try to cut everything at once. Start by tracking what you spend. It’s worth doing even if you don’t like the answer.”

reading.title: Phones Down, Doors Open
paragraphs: Two years ago, nineteen-year-old Jahongir spent up to eight hours a day on his phone. “I had hundreds of online friends,” he says, “but I didn’t know the name of the old man who lived next door.” When that neighbour, a retired doctor called Mirzaakbar aka, fell ill and nobody noticed for two days, Jahongir felt terrible. “I still wish I had knocked on his door earlier.”

With three friends, he started a small project called “Eshik oçiq” (“Open Door”). Young volunteers visit elderly people in their mahalla once a week. They help with shopping, fix small things around the house and, most importantly, sit and talk. Some of the volunteers teach the older people how to make video calls to their grandchildren abroad. In return, the older people share stories about their lives, recipes and even advice about exams.

The project now has more than sixty volunteers in four districts of Tashkent. Not everyone was enthusiastic at first. Some parents wished their children would spend the time studying instead. But teachers say the volunteers have become more confident and responsible. Jahongir still uses social media, but differently. “If only I had understood earlier that the internet can bring people together in real life,” he says. “Now we use it to find out who needs help.”

reading.title: A Letter to Myself in 2035
paragraphs: Every year Mr Rahimov, an English teacher in Jizzakh, asks his final-year students to write a letter to themselves ten years in the future. He keeps the letters in a box and posts them back to the students a decade later. This is part of the letter that Kamila wrote last spring.

“Dear Kamila of 2035, by the time you read this, you will have finished medical school — I hope! You will probably be working in a children’s hospital, because that has been my dream since I was nine. I wonder if you will have learned to drive yet. Right now I’m terrified of it. I also hope you will have visited Japan, which I have wanted to see since I first watched those old animated films with my brother.

“I imagine that on a normal weekday you will be checking on small patients, drinking too much coffee and complaining about the night shifts. Please don’t forget why you started. And please call Mum more often than I do now. If you have changed your plans completely, that’s fine too — as long as you are doing something that makes you proud. Love, Kamila (aged 17)”

writing.modelAnswerEn: Dear Mr Yusupov, I’m writing to update you on today’s meeting with Green Valley Foods. Ms Karimova said that they were happy with the quality of our packaging, but she explained that two deliveries had arrived late in March. She told me that their warehouse had been full and that this had caused extra costs. She asked if we could deliver smaller amounts more often, and she wanted to know what the price would be for weekly deliveries. She also asked whether we had ever worked with frozen products. I said that I would check with our logistics team. Finally, she asked us to send a new offer by Friday and not to change the delivery address without telling her. Could you let me know if you would like me to prepare the offer? I hope you are feeling better. Best regards, Sevara

writing.modelAnswerEn: A Review of “Yo’lda”, a Public Transport App. I have been using Yo’lda, which was launched in Tashkent two years ago, almost every day. The app shows exactly where each bus is, so I no longer wait at the stop for twenty minutes. The feature that I find most useful is the alarm which reminds me when my stop is near. It is ideal for students and office workers who travel at busy times, and for visitors who don’t know the city. However, the app has some weaknesses. It uses a lot of battery, and the information about minibuses, which are very popular in our area, is often missing. Users whose phones are old also complain that it is slow. Overall, I would recommend it to anyone who uses public transport regularly, because it saves both time and stress.

writing.modelAnswerEn: Dear Sir or Madam, I am writing to complain about the decision to replace the park on Bog‘bon Street with a car park. Since the park was closed, children have had nowhere to play, and older residents have lost the only quiet place where they used to meet. In summer the street has become much hotter, because the trees which gave shade have gone. If the council had asked local people for their opinion, it would have learned how important the park was. You should have looked for another place for the car park; the empty land behind the market could have been used instead. If more trees had been kept, the area would not have become so hot. However, it is not too late. I suggest that the council plant trees along the car park and create a small playground at its edge. I look forward to your reply. Yours faithfully, Zarina Tokhtaeva

writing.modelAnswerEn: As soon as I got off the bus, I realised that something was wrong. The bag that had been sitting next to me for six hours was still on the seat — and the bus was already driving away. My passport, money and phone were all inside it. While I was standing in the dusty square in Termez wondering what to do, a young man came up to me. He had seen the whole thing from his shop. Without saying much, he made a phone call, and ten minutes later a taxi arrived. We chased the bus through the town, and by the time we caught it at the next stop, the driver had already found my bag and put it aside. I had been panicking for nearly half an hour, but suddenly I was laughing with two complete strangers. Eventually the young man refused to take any money for the taxi. I will never forget the kindness I met that afternoon.

checklistUz: Qiziqarli sarlavha va kiriş (savol yoki hayotiy misol).
Uç-tört aniq maslahat, har biri alohida paragrafda.
Gerund va infinitive andozalari töğri işlatilgan.
Öquvçiga “siz” orqali murojaat, samimiy ohang.
Qisqa xulosa.

“avoid + -ing” andozasini işlating.

writing.modelAnswerEn: Where Does Your Stipend Go? Many first-year students are surprised to find that their money disappears in the first ten days of the month. Here are four tips that really work. First, try to write down everything you spend for two weeks. It’s worth doing even if the results are embarrassing, because you cannot fix what you cannot see. Second, avoid buying lunch every day. Cooking with your flatmates is cheaper and, honestly, more fun. Third, if you can’t afford to go out with friends, suggest doing something free, like walking in the park or watching a film at home. Real friends won’t mind. Finally, never agree to lend money you need yourself, and stop using your card for small payments you don’t notice. In short, managing money isn’t about saying no to everything — it’s about deciding what really matters to you.

writing.promptEn: “Young people today are less connected to their communities than their parents were.” Write an essay giving your opinion, with examples, and suggest what could be done.
writing.instructionUz: “Bugungi yoşlar ota-onalariga qaraganda öz jamoasidan uzoqlaşgan” degan fikr haqida esse yozing: fikringiz, misollar va nima qiliş mumkinligi. Wish / if only ni kamida ikki marta (bitta hozirgi, bitta ötmiş haqida) işlating.
checklistUz: Kirişda mavzu va fikringiz.
Ikki asosiy paragraf: sabablar va misollar.
Qarşi fikrni tan oliş (Some people argue that …).
Wish / if only kamida ikki marta.
Taklif va xulosa.

mustInclude.whyUz: Istak yoki afsusni “I wish …” bilan bildiring.
Qarşi fikrni “However, …” bilan bering.
Esse xulosa bilan tugaydi.

writing.modelAnswerEn: It is often said that young people today care more about their phones than about their neighbours. In my opinion, this is partly true. When my parents were young, they knew everyone in the mahalla, and weddings and repairs were shared by the whole street. Today many teenagers live in apartment blocks where they rarely talk to the people next door. I sometimes wish I knew more about the families on my floor. However, it would be unfair to say that young people do not care. During the floods last spring, students organised food collections online in a few hours, which shows that technology can connect people as well as divide them. The problem is that these connections often stay online. If only schools had encouraged volunteering when I was younger, I might have discovered it earlier. In conclusion, young people are not less caring, but they need more chances to turn online interest into real action in their communities.

writing.promptEn: Write a letter to yourself in ten years’ time. Say what you hope you will have achieved, what you will probably be doing on a normal day, and what you hope you won’t have forgotten.
writing.instructionUz: Ön yildan keyingi özingizga xat yozing: nimalarga erişgan bölişingizni umid qilasiz, oddiy kunda ehtimol nima bilan band bölasiz va nimani unutmagan bölişingizni istaysiz. Future Perfect’ni kamida uç marta, Future Continuous’ni kamida ikki marta işlating.
checklistUz: Murojaat (Dear … of 2036,) va samimiy yakun.
Erişilgan maqsadlar Future Perfect bilan (By then you will have …).
Oddiy kun Future Continuous bilan (You will probably be …).
Bitta ögit yoki iltimos (Please don’t forget …).
Hozirgi holatingiz bilan solişturma.

mustInclude.whyUz: Erişilgan natija — “will have + V3”.
Kelajakdagi oddiy kun — “will be + -ing”.
“By then …” iborasi bilan vaqt nuqtasini belgilang.

writing.modelAnswerEn: Dear Bekzod of 2036, by the time you read this, you will be thirty-four. I hope you will have finished your engineering degree and that you will have found a job designing solar power stations, because that is what excites me most right now. You will probably be living in Tashkent, and on a normal morning you will be driving to work while listening to the same old songs. By then you will have travelled to at least five countries — at the moment I have only been to Kazakhstan. I hope you won’t have forgotten how hard it was to pass maths in tenth grade, and how much Mr Saidov helped. Please call him and say thank you. Most of all, I hope you will still be playing football on Sundays with the guys from our street. Don’t become too serious. Your younger self, Bekzod

speaking.questionEn: Tell me about an important conversation you had recently. What did the other person say and ask?
speaking.hintUz: Özlaştirma gap işlating: “She told me that …”, “He asked me whether …”, “They asked me to …”.
speaking.textAlternative: Yaqinda bölgan muhim suhbatni özlaştirma gaplar bilan 7–8 gapda yozing.
followUpsEn: How did you react?
Would you change anything you said?

speaking.questionEn: Describe a misunderstanding at work, school or in your family. How was it solved?
speaking.hintUz: Kim nima deganini va nima tuşunilganini solişturing: “I thought he had said …, but he had actually said …”.
speaking.textAlternative: Bitta anglaşilmovçilik va uning yeçimi haqida 7 gap yozing.
followUpsEn: What did you learn from it?
How can people avoid misunderstandings?

speaking.questionEn: What makes someone a good communicator at work? Give examples.
speaking.hintUz: Ikki-uç xususiyatni ayting va har biriga hayotdan misol keltiring.
speaking.textAlternative: Işda yaxşi muloqot qila oladigan odam haqida 7 gap yozing.
followUpsEn: Is it better to write or to call?
How should you give negative feedback?

speaking.questionEn: What invention of the last fifty years has been most useful for people in your country? Why?
speaking.hintUz: Ixtironi relative clause bilan tasvirlang: “It’s a device which …”, “People who … benefit most.”
speaking.textAlternative: Sizningça eng foydali ixtiro haqida 7–8 gap yozing.
followUpsEn: Are there any negative effects?
How did people live before it?

speaking.questionEn: Describe an app or service that would solve a problem in your town.
speaking.hintUz: Muammo, yeçim va foydalanuvçilarni ayting: “It would be an app that …, for people who …”.
speaking.textAlternative: Şahringiz muammosini hal qiladigan ilova ğoyasi haqida 7 gap yozing.
followUpsEn: How would you make money?
Who would be your first users?

speaking.questionEn: Should people worry about how apps use their personal data?
speaking.hintUz: Ikki tomonni körib çiqing va öz fikringizni misol bilan asoslang.
speaking.textAlternative: Ilovalar şaxsiy ma’lumotlardan qanday foydalanişi haqida fikringizni 7 gapda yozing.
followUpsEn: Do you read privacy policies?
What information would you never share?

speaking.questionEn: Tell me about a decision you regret. What would have happened if you had decided differently?
speaking.hintUz: “I should have …” bilan boşlang va “If I had …, I would have …” bilan natijani tasavvur qiling.
speaking.textAlternative: Afsuslangan bir qaroringiz va boşqa yöl tanlaganingizda nima bölişi haqida 7 gap yozing.
followUpsEn: What did you learn from it?
Would you give the same advice to a friend?

speaking.questionEn: Describe an environmental problem in your region. How could it have been avoided?
speaking.hintUz: Muammoni tasvirlang, keyin “If people had …, …” va “The authorities should have …” tuzilmalari.
speaking.textAlternative: Viloyatingizdagi ekologik muammo va uni qanday oldini oliş mumkin edi — 7 gap yozing.
followUpsEn: Who is responsible?
What can young people do now?

speaking.questionEn: Talk about a time when something could have gone wrong but didn’t.
speaking.hintUz: “It could have been much worse …” va “If I hadn’t …, I might have …” tuzilmalari.
speaking.textAlternative: Yomon tugaşi mumkin bölgan, lekin yaxşi tugagan voqea haqida 7 gap yozing.
followUpsEn: How did you feel afterwards?
Who helped you?

speaking.questionEn: Tell me about something unexpected that happened to you on a journey.
speaking.hintUz: Fonni Past Continuous bilan, oldinroq bölganini Past Perfect bilan bering: “I had been …ing when …”.
speaking.textAlternative: Safarda kutilmaganda bölgan voqea haqida 8 gap yozing.
followUpsEn: How did you feel at that moment?
What would you do differently?

speaking.questionEn: Describe a time when a stranger helped you or you helped a stranger.
speaking.hintUz: Voqea ketma-ketligini aniq qiling: when, while, as soon as, eventually.
speaking.textAlternative: Notaniş odam yordam bergan yoki siz yordam bergan vaziyat haqida 7 gap yozing.
followUpsEn: Why do you think they helped?
Is hospitality changing in modern cities?

speaking.questionEn: What was your first trip without your parents like? What had you expected, and what was different?
speaking.hintUz: “I had expected …, but in fact …” tuzilmasidan foydalaning.
speaking.textAlternative: Ota-onasiz birinçi safaringiz haqida 7 gap yozing: nimani kutgan edingiz va nima boşqaça bölib çiqdi.
followUpsEn: What did you learn about yourself?
Where would you like to travel next?

speaking.questionEn: What do you do to save money? What have you stopped doing or decided to do?
speaking.hintUz: “I’ve stopped …ing”, “I’ve decided to …”, “I try to avoid …ing” tuzilmalari.
speaking.textAlternative: Pul tejaş uçun nima qilişingiz haqida 7 gap yozing.
followUpsEn: What is your biggest expense?
Is it difficult for young people to save?

speaking.questionEn: Do you prefer paying in cash or by card or phone? Why?
speaking.hintUz: Ikkala usulning afzallik va kamçiligini solişturing, keyin öz tanlovingizni ayting.
speaking.textAlternative: Naqd va karta orqali tölovni solişturib, 7 gap yozing.
followUpsEn: How do older people in your family pay?
How can people protect themselves from scams?

speaking.questionEn: What is the best piece of advice about money that someone has given you?
speaking.hintUz: “My grandfather advised me to …”, “He told me to avoid …ing” — maslahat va natijasini ayting.
speaking.textAlternative: Pul haqida olgan eng yaxşi maslahatingiz haqida 7 gap yozing.
followUpsEn: Do you follow this advice?
What would you tell a younger brother or sister?

speaking.questionEn: What do you wish you could change about the place where you live?
speaking.hintUz: “I wish there were …”, “I wish people would …”, “If only …” tuzilmalari bilan ikki-uç fikr ayting.
speaking.textAlternative: Yaşaydigan joyingizda nimani özgartirişni xohlaşingiz haqida 7 gap yozing.
followUpsEn: Who could make this change?
What could you do yourself?

speaking.questionEn: Is there anything you wish you had done differently at school?
speaking.hintUz: “I wish I had …” / “If only I hadn’t …” bilan boşlang va nima uçun ekanini tuşuntiring.
speaking.textAlternative: Maktab yillaringizda boşqaça qilişni istagan narsangiz haqida 7 gap yozing.
followUpsEn: What advice would you give to school students today?
Is it ever too late to change?

speaking.questionEn: Should volunteering be part of every school programme? Why or why not?
speaking.hintUz: Ikkala tomonni körib çiqing va aniq misol keltiring.
speaking.textAlternative: Köngillilik maktab dasturiga kiritilişi haqida fikringizni 7 gapda yozing.
followUpsEn: Have you ever volunteered?
What kind of volunteering is most useful?

speaking.questionEn: Where do you think you will be in ten years? What will you have achieved?
speaking.hintUz: “In ten years’ time I’ll be …ing” va “By then I’ll have …” tuzilmalari.
speaking.textAlternative: Ön yildan keyingi hayotingiz haqida 7 gap yozing.
followUpsEn: What might stop you?
Who will help you?

speaking.questionEn: How will your city have changed by 2040? What will people be doing differently?
speaking.hintUz: Transport, uylar, iş va ekologiya haqida başorat qiling: “By 2040 they will have built …”.
speaking.textAlternative: Şahringiz 2040-yilda qanday bölişi haqida 7 gap yozing.
followUpsEn: Which change would you like most?
What should not change?

speaking.questionEn: What will you be doing at this time next week? What will you have done by then?
speaking.hintUz: Bitta aniq vaqt tanlang va ikkala zamonni işlating.
speaking.textAlternative: Kelasi haftadagi rejalaringiz haqida Future Continuous va Future Perfect bilan 6 gap yozing.
followUpsEn: Is your week usually busy?
How do you plan your time?

exercises.instructionUz: Sözning ma’nosini tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: postpone — keyinga qoldirmoq.
exercises.question: What does “postpone” mean?

exercises.instructionUz: Özlaştirma gapni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: can → could.
exercises.question: “I can help you.” → He said he ___ help me.

exercises.instructionUz: Böş joyga say yoki tell ning töğri şaklini yozing.
exercises.explanationUz: Kişi bor (us) — told.
exercises.text: She ___ us that the price had changed.

exercises.instructionUz: Töğri gapni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Özlaştirilgan söroqda darak tartibi: if I was ready.
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: He asked me was I ready.
He asked me if I was ready.
He asked me if was I ready.
He asked to me if I was ready.

exercises.instructionUz: Gapni ingliz tiliga özlaştirma gap bilan tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: Buyruq: told + kişi + to + fe’l.
exercises.source: Rahbar menga hisobotni juma kunigaça yuborişni aytdi.
accepted: The manager told me to send the report by Friday
My manager told me to send the report by Friday
The boss told me to send the report by Friday
The manager asked me to send the report by Friday

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlardan özlaştirma söroq gap tuzing.
exercises.explanationUz: asked + kişi + wh-söz + ega + fe’l: She asked me where I worked.

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlarni tarjimasi bilan boğlang.
exercises.explanationUz: deny — inkor etmoq, confirm — tasdiqlamoq, complaint — şikoyat, deal — bitim.

exercises.instructionUz: Grammatik qoida haqidagi fikr töğrimi (true) yoki xatomi (false)?
exercises.explanationUz: Gap hali ham töğri bölsa (ofis hali ham soat 9 da oçiladi), zamonni özgartirmaslik mumkin. Fikr töğri.
exercises.statement: If something is still true, we can keep the present tense: “He said the office opens at nine.”

exercises.instructionUz: Sözning ma’nosini tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: affordable — hamyonbop.
exercises.question: What does “affordable” mean?

exercises.instructionUz: Mos olmoşni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Egalik — whose.
exercises.question: The student ___ project won the competition is from Navoi.

exercises.instructionUz: Böş joyga mos olmoşni yozing.
exercises.explanationUz: Joy — where.
exercises.text: This is the office ___ the app was designed.

exercises.instructionUz: Töğri gapni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Izohlovçi gapda narsa uçun which; that va who işlatilmaydi, it takrorlanmaydi.
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: My laptop, that I bought in May, is broken.
My laptop, who I bought in May, is broken.
My laptop, which I bought in May, is broken.
My laptop, which I bought it in May, is broken.

exercises.instructionUz: Gapni ingliz tiliga tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: “… bilan işlaydigan odamlar” — people who work with …
exercises.source: Kompyuter bilan işlaydigan odamlar köp dam olişi kerak.
accepted: People who work with computers should rest a lot
People who work with computers need to rest a lot
People who work on computers should rest a lot
People that work with computers should rest a lot

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlardan gap tuzing.
exercises.explanationUz: ot + (that) + ega + fe’l: The phone I bought is light.

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlarni tarjimasi bilan boğlang.
exercises.explanationUz: launch — işga tuşirmoq, feature — xususiyat, investor — sarmoyador, privacy — maxfiylik.

exercises.instructionUz: Grammatik qoida haqidagi fikr töğrimi (true) yoki xatomi (false)?
exercises.explanationUz: Olmoş EGA bölganda taşlab bölmaydi: The man who called … Fikr xato.
exercises.statement: We can always leave out “who” in “The man who called you is here.”

exercises.instructionUz: Sözning ma’nosini tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: drought — qurğoqçilik.
exercises.question: What does “drought” mean?

exercises.instructionUz: Mos şaklni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Ötmişdagi natija — would have + V3.
exercises.question: If we had taken a map, we ___ lost.

exercises.instructionUz: Fe’lni töğri şaklda yozing (should have + V3).
exercises.explanationUz: should have + V3: should have gone.
exercises.text: You look ill. You ___ (go) to bed earlier.

exercises.instructionUz: Töğri gapni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: If + had + V3, … would have + V3.
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: If it hadn’t rained, we would have played.
If it wouldn’t have rained, we would have played.
If it didn’t rain, we would have played.
If it hadn’t rained, we would played.

exercises.instructionUz: Gapni ingliz tiliga tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: “… mumkin edi” — could have + V3.
exercises.source: Bu juda yomonroq bölişi mumkin edi.
accepted: It could have been much worse
This could have been much worse
It could have been a lot worse
It could have been far worse

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlardan gap tuzing.
exercises.explanationUz: ega + shouldn’t have + V3 + …

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlarni tarjimasi bilan boğlang.
exercises.explanationUz: prevent — oldini olmoq, consequence — oqibat, restore — tiklamoq, flood — toşqin.

exercises.instructionUz: Grammatik qoida haqidagi fikr töğrimi (true) yoki xatomi (false)?
exercises.explanationUz: “I’d gone” = I had gone; “I’d have gone” = I would have gone. Fikr töğri.
exercises.statement: In “If I’d known, I’d have helped”, the first ’d means “had” and the second means “would”.

exercises.instructionUz: Sözning ma’nosini tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: hospitality — mehmondöstlik.
exercises.question: What does “hospitality” mean?

exercises.instructionUz: Mos zamonni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Fon jarayon — was raining.
exercises.question: It ___ heavily when we left the hotel.

exercises.instructionUz: Fe’lni Past Perfect şaklida yozing.
exercises.explanationUz: Avvalroq bölgan voqea: had forgotten.
exercises.text: At the airport I realised that I ___ (forget) my charger.

exercises.instructionUz: Töğri gapni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Know — holat fe’li: I knew (I was knowing — xato).
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: I was knowing nobody in the city.
I knew nobody in the city.
I was know nobody in the city.

exercises.instructionUz: Gapni ingliz tiliga tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: “… yetib kelgunimizça … yopilgan edi” — By the time we arrived, … had closed.
exercises.source: Biz yetib kelgunimizça muzey yopilgan edi.
accepted: By the time we arrived, the museum had closed
By the time we got there, the museum had closed
When we arrived, the museum had closed
By the time we arrived the museum had closed
When we arrived, the museum had already closed

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlardan gap tuzing.
exercises.explanationUz: ega + had been + V-ing + for …

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlarni tarjimasi bilan boğlang.
exercises.explanationUz: luggage — yuk, stranger — notaniş odam, delay — keçikiş, eventually — oxir-oqibat.

exercises.instructionUz: Grammatik qoida haqidagi fikr töğrimi (true) yoki xatomi (false)?
exercises.explanationUz: Before / after bilan tartib aniq bölsa, Past Simple ham yetarli. Fikr töğri.
exercises.statement: In “After we ate, we walked to the square”, the Past Perfect is not necessary.

exercises.instructionUz: Sözning ma’nosini tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: income — daromad.
exercises.question: What does “income” mean?

exercises.instructionUz: Mos şaklni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Consider + -ing.
exercises.question: Have you considered ___ a cheaper phone plan?

exercises.instructionUz: Fe’lni töğri şaklda yozing.
exercises.explanationUz: Refuse + to: refused to sign.
exercises.text: He ___ (refuse) ___ (sign) the contract.

exercises.instructionUz: Töğri gapni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Look forward to + -ing.
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: I look forward to hear from you.
I look forward to hearing from you.
I look forward hearing from you.
I look forward for hearing from you.

exercises.instructionUz: Gapni ingliz tiliga tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: “Qurbimiz yetmaydi” — can’t afford to.
exercises.source: Biz yangi maşina olişga qurbimiz yetmaydi.
accepted: We can’t afford to buy a new car
We can't afford to buy a new car
We cannot afford to buy a new car
We can’t afford a new car

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlardan gap tuzing.
exercises.explanationUz: avoid + -ing.

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlarni tarjimasi bilan boğlang.
exercises.explanationUz: loan — kredit, savings — jamğarma, scam — firibgarlik, budget — byudjet.

exercises.instructionUz: Grammatik qoida haqidagi fikr töğrimi (true) yoki xatomi (false)?
exercises.explanationUz: “I stopped to buy bread” — non sotib oliş uçun töxtadim; “stopped buying” — sotib olişni taşladim. Ma’no farq qiladi — fikr xato.
exercises.statement: “I stopped to buy bread” and “I stopped buying bread” mean the same.

exercises.instructionUz: Sözning ma’nosini tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: volunteer — köngilli.
exercises.question: What does “volunteer” mean?

exercises.instructionUz: Mos şaklni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Hozirgi istak — Past Simple (lived).
exercises.question: I wish my best friend ___ in the same city.

exercises.instructionUz: Fe’lni töğri şaklda yozing.
exercises.explanationUz: Ötmişdagi afsus — had + V3: had taken.
exercises.text: I wish I ___ (take) more photos at my sister’s wedding.

exercises.instructionUz: Töğri gapni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Özimiz haqida would emas, could: I wish I could …
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: I wish I would speak Chinese.
I wish I could speak Chinese.
I wish I can speak Chinese.
I wish I will speak Chinese.

exercises.instructionUz: Gapni ingliz tiliga tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: Boşqa odamning odati — wish + would (not).
exercises.source: Qaniydi, odamlar köçaga axlat taşlamasa.
accepted: I wish people wouldn’t throw rubbish in the street
I wish people wouldn't throw rubbish in the street
I wish people would not throw rubbish in the street
I wish people wouldn’t throw rubbish on the street
If only people wouldn’t throw rubbish in the street

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlardan gap tuzing.
exercises.explanationUz: wish + ega + would + fe’l.

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlarni tarjimasi bilan boğlang.
exercises.explanationUz: community — jamoa, donate — xayriya qilmoq, fair — adolatli, pressure — bosim.

exercises.instructionUz: Grammatik qoida haqidagi fikr töğrimi (true) yoki xatomi (false)?
exercises.explanationUz: Ertangi imtihon — real kelajak: hope. Wish bu yerda xato. Fikr töğri.
exercises.statement: We say “I hope you pass your exam tomorrow”, not “I wish you passed”.

exercises.instructionUz: Sözning ma’nosini tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: priority — ustuvor vazifa.
exercises.question: What does “priority” mean?

exercises.instructionUz: Mos şaklni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: By + vaqtgaça tugagan — will have + V3.
exercises.question: By Monday, the builders ___ the new bridge.

exercises.instructionUz: Fe’lni Future Continuous şaklida yozing.
exercises.explanationUz: will be + V-ing: will be travelling.
exercises.text: Don’t visit us in July — we ___ (travel) around Europe.

exercises.instructionUz: Töğri gapni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Will have + V3 (gone).
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: By ten, everyone will have went home.
By ten, everyone will have gone home.
By ten, everyone will gone home.
By ten, everyone will be gone home already.

exercises.instructionUz: Gapni ingliz tiliga tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: “Aynan şu paytda … ayotgan bölaman” — This time … I will be + V-ing.

This time tomorrow I will be taking my exam
At this time tomorrow I will be taking an exam
This time tomorrow I’ll be taking an exam
Tomorrow at this time I will be taking an exam

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlardan muloyim söroq tuzing.
exercises.explanationUz: Will + ega + be + V-ing …?

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlarni tarjimasi bilan boğlang.
exercises.explanationUz: goal — maqsad, predict — başorat qilmoq, graduate — öqişni tamomlamoq, long-term — uzoq muddatli.

exercises.instructionUz: Grammatik qoida haqidagi fikr töğrimi (true) yoki xatomi (false)?
exercises.explanationUz: “Will you be using …?” odatda “Will you use …?” dan muloyimroq eşitiladi. Fikr töğri.
exercises.statement: “Will you be using the car?” sounds more polite than “Will you use the car?”.
